questions.question:
**In the following question, some parts of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate**** ****option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'.** 

Sameer is the most succeeded of all (1)/ the businessmen (2)/ in this city today. (3)/ No Error (4)

options.text: Sameer is the most succeeded of all

questions.solution:
The error is in part** 1)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Here the error lies in the usage of the word **"succeeded" **in its place "**successful**" will be used.
 
• **succeeded**(**verb**) is wrong here because we are not showing any working activity.
 
• **successful**(**adjective**) will be used here because we are showing the quality of businessmen.

Hence, the correct sentence will be:-Sameer is the most** successful** of all the businessmen in this city.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Verb-** these are the words that **show the time **in the sentence. They are also used to tell us about **something is happening** in the sentence. Eg: Run(Ram runs), Flies(Plane flies), Slept(Sita slept).
 
• **Adjective- **these are the words that qualify Noun or Pronoun in a sentence. Eg: Large(Large man), Heavy(Heavy man)

questions.question:
What will come in place of question mark (?) in the given equation?

12 ? 10 ? 8 = 14
questions.solution:
After insertion of the signs in the given equation:

1) – and + → 12 - 10 + 8 = 10 ≠ 14

2) + and ÷ → 12 + 10 ÷ 8 = 13.25 ≠ 14

3) × and + → 12 × 10 + 8 = 128 ≠ 14

4) + and – → 12 + 10 – 8 = 14

Hence, + and – is the correct answer.

questions.question: Weight of A is half of B. Weight of B is 3 times of C. Weight of C is one-fourth of D. Weight of D is 5 times of E. Who is the heaviest?

questions.question: What is the highest common factor of 48, 120 and 240?
questions.solution:
Prime factors of 48 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 3 = 2 × 24

Prime factors of 120 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 3 × 5 = 5 × 24

Prime factors of 240 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 3 × 5 = 10 × 24

⇒ highest common factor of 48, 120 and 240 is 24

questions.question: After giving a discount of 33.33%, there is a loss of 11.111%. If only 10% discount is given, then what will be the profit percentage?
questions.solution:
Let the marked price (M.P) = x

After a discount of 33.33%

Selling price = S.P = (1 - 0.3333) × x = 0.6667x

Loss percentage = (loss/C.P) × 100 = {(C.P - S.P)/C.P} × 100

Loss% = 11.111%

⇒ (C.P - 0.6667x)/C.P} × 100 = 11.111

⇒ 1 - 0.6667x/C.P = 0.11111

⇒ 0.6667x/C.P = 0.88889

⇒ C.P = 0.6667x/0.88889 = 0.75x

When only 10% discount was given

S.P = (1 - 0.1) × x = 0.9x

Profit = S.P - C.P = 0.9x - 0.75x = 0.15x

Profit% = (profit/C.P) × 100

⇒ profit % = (0.15x/0.75x) × 100 = 20%

**Alternate Solution:**

33.33% = 1/3

Ratio of MP to SP = 3: (3 - 1) = (3: 2) × 4 = 12: 8 ---(A)

11.11% = 1/9

Ratio of CP to SP = 9: (9 - 1) = (9: 8) × 1 = 9: 8 --- (B)

If discount is 10% then Ratio of MP to SP = 10: 9 ---- (C)

Make MP same in A and C, new ratio of A and C = 60 : 40 and 60: 54 Now making SP of B equal to new ratio of A, = 45: 40

So CP = 45 unit and SP = 54 unit

Profit = (9/45) × 100 = 20%

Cost of new liquid = (x) × 52 + (1 - x) × 65 = 65 - 13x

Cost of mixture = 60/litre

⇒ 65 - 13x = 60

⇒ 13x = 5

⇒ x = 5/13

⇒ (1 - x) = 1 - 5/13 = 8/13

The ratio in which liquids must be mixed = x/(1 - x) = (5/13)/(8/13) = 5/8 = 5∶ 8

Price of cheaper = Rs. 52/litres

Price of dearer = Rs. 65/litre

Mean price = Rs. 60/litre

Required ratio = Quantity of cheaper/quantity of dearer

Required ratio = (65 - 60)/(60 - 52) = 5/8 = 5 ∶ 8

questions.question: A train crosses a platform in 30 seconds travelling with a speed of 72 km/hr. If the length of the train be 120 metres, then what will be the length (in metres) of the platform?
questions.solution:
Speed = distance/time

Distance = speed × time

Speed = 72 km/hr

Time = 30 sec = 30/(60 × 60) = 1/120 hr

Distance travelled by train in 30 sec = 72 × (1/120) = 0.6 km = 600m

Distance travelled by train = length of platform + length of train

⇒ length of platform = 600 - 120 = 480 m

**Shortcut method:**

Length of platform = (speed × time) - length of train

⇒ length of platform = {72 × (30/3600)} - 120/1000 = 0.48 km = 480 m

questions.question: The speed of a boat is 3 km/hr in still water and the speed of the stream is 1 km/hr. If the boat takes 9 hours to go to a place and come back, then what is the distance (in km) of the place?
questions.solution:
Speed of boat in still water = B = 3 km/hr

Speed of stream = S = 1 km/hr

Speed of boat going downstream = B + S = 3 + 1 = 4 km/hr

Speed of boat going upstream = B - S = 3 - 1 = 2 km/hr

Let the distance of the place be d.

Time taken to go to that place = Distance/Speed of boat downstream = d/4 hr

Time taken to come back from that place = Distance/Speed of boat upstream = d/2 hr

Total time taken to go and come back to that place = 9 hr

⇒ d/4 + d/2 = 9

⇒ 3d/4 = 9

⇒ d = 12 km

questions.question: Who invented Airplane?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Wright Brothers.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Wright Brothers:**

 
 
• Orville and Wilbur Wright (The Wright Brothers) invented the first aeroplane in 1903. 
 
• In order to make a biplane roll to the right or left, Wilbur came up with a straightforward solution in 1899.
 
• They used a kite to test the system before moving on to many gliders.
 
• The Wrights' first two gliders, which were flown in 1900 and 1901, didn't perform as well as they'd intended.
 
• The gliders were difficult to fully control and did not offer an adequate lift.
 
• In order to find the ideal wing form for an aeroplane, Wilbur and Orville constructed a wind tunnel and ran tests over the winter of 1901-1902.
 
• The Wrights developed a gasoline engine that was both light and strong enough to power an aeroplane during the winter of 1902-03 with the assistance of their mechanic, Charlie Taylor.
 
• They also developed a brand-new, powered aircraft and created the first real aeroplane propellers.
 
• The first prolonged, controlled flights in a powered aircraft were accomplished by Wilbur and Orville Wright on December 17, 1903.
 
• They took four flights on that day.
 
• The first Wright Flyer flight was made by Orville.
 
• The day's fourth trip was flown by Wilbur.
 
• The first practicable aeroplane in history was the 1905 Wright Flyer.
